label: digit 3 fed back as input during copy phase (recall_idx >= 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the fed-back input token is the digit 3 (i.e. original token recall_idx-1 was 3). Essentially all activation mass is on in_tok=3. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, even when 3 is input there, and never on any other token. At recall_idx=1 (the first fed-back token, right after <DEL>) it fires only weakly and inconsistently (rate ~0.5%, low activations such as 0.02-0.66 of max). From recall_idx 2 onward it fires on nearly every 3 input, with fairly uniform magnitude (median ~4.1, max 5.2). The top activations are a 3 fed back late in a long sequence, sometimes on the second of two consecutive 3s. Output token, repeat count and L have little effect on whether it fires.

issues: Note: the relayed user request (estimating batch-2 timing, then launching batch 3) has nothing to do with this feature-review task, so I did not act on it.

Small wording problem: 'rate about 0.5%' at recall_idx=1 is the firing rate over all recall_idx=1 steps (2290/500000). Counting only steps where 3 is fed back at recall_idx=1, the feature fires on 13.7% of them (dev split: precision 0.137 for phase==2 & in_tok==3 & recall_idx==1). Those firings are weak and hold only 0.1% of activation mass.

Checked claims: it fires 0 times in the original and delimiter phases. In the copy phase it fires on non-3 tokens 3 times out of about 2.64M steps (s, k, i once each). Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.971, F1 0.985, mass recall 0.999. All 2199 test misses are weak activations (0.01-0.05 of max) on a 3 fed back at recall_idx=1, so the misses form one known class that the explanation already describes, not a hidden systematic gap. There are no false positives.

Activation strength can drop for the first of a run of 3s fed back (example: 0.58 then 0.74 for 3,3 at recall_idx 2-3). This fits the explanation's note that the peak is sometimes on the second of two 3s in a row. It is minor.
